questions.q: What does the balance sheet report, and over what timeframe?
options: Revenue and expenses over a full fiscal year
Only cash transactions over the past week
Assets, liabilities, and equity as of a single specific date
Projected earnings for the next five years
questions.explain: The balance sheet is a snapshot of assets, liabilities, and equity at one specific point in time, dated 'as of [date].'

questions.q: Why is the balance sheet described as a 'photograph' compared to the income statement's 'video'?
options: Because the balance sheet captures a single instant, while the income statement covers a span of time
Because the balance sheet includes actual photographs of company assets
Because the income statement is always shorter than the balance sheet
There is no meaningful difference between the two
questions.explain: The balance sheet is dated as of one moment, while the income statement covers an entire period, like a month, quarter, or year.

questions.q: In a correctly prepared balance sheet, what must always be true?
options: Total Assets must always be larger than Total Liabilities and Equity
Total Assets must exactly equal Total Liabilities plus Total Equity
Total Liabilities must always equal Total Equity
There is no required relationship between the totals
questions.explain: The balance sheet is literally the accounting equation (Assets = Liabilities + Equity) formatted as a report, so the two totals must always match.

questions.q: Where does the Retained Earnings figure on the balance sheet come from?
options: It is arbitrarily chosen by management each year
It is always equal to Total Assets
It has no connection to the income statement
It is the result of the roll-forward calculation: beginning balance, plus net income from the income statement, minus dividends paid
questions.explain: Retained Earnings is built from the exact roll-forward calculation covered in lessons 11 and 25 — it is not an independently chosen number.

questions.q: What is the simplest sanity check anyone can run on a balance sheet?
options: Checking that every account has a positive balance
Confirming that cash is the largest account on the report
Confirming that Total Assets equals Total Liabilities plus Total Equity
Confirming that no account appears more than once
questions.explain: If a balance sheet doesn't balance (Assets = Liabilities + Equity), something upstream is definitively wrong — this is the most basic check available.
